Gary and Barbra have fallen out of favor in the US, according to baby-name research published in 2013.
Gary peaked at No. 9 in 1952, with about 38,000 registrations, but only around 400 babies were named Gary in 2013.
Barbra Streisand’s spelling peaked at No. 511 in the 1960s and left the top 1,000 in 1971; Barbara now barely makes the list.
Llewellyn and Claudine have also declined, with Claudine dropping off the US charts in 1975.

An Arizona State University graduate student discovered a 2.8-million-year-old jawbone in Ethiopia’s Afar region in 2013.
The fossil is the oldest known evidence of the Homo genus, predating previously known Homo fossils by about 400,000 years.
Its features link Australopithecus afarensis with later Homo, helping illuminate a poorly understood period in human evolution.
Researchers say its owner walked upright and lived in a dry climate; diet and possible stone-tool use remain under study.

A highly pathogenic H5N2 bird flu strain devastated a commercial flock of 15,000 turkeys in Pope County, Minnesota, with fewer than 100 birds alive by Thursday.

An external committee of 11 experts said in a report on CDC lab safety that the agency’s safety commitment is “inconsistent and insufficient” and its training inadequate.  
The report, completed in January and posted on the CDC website this week, followed lab incidents involving anthrax, avian influenza and Ebola.  
The committee recommended external reviews and accreditation for all CDC labs, along with standardized training, risk assessments and a director to oversee safety.  
The CDC formed the advisory group in July, and Chief Operating Officer Sherri Berger said many improvements were already underway.
